issues.title: [BACKEND][NV] Lower float rem to libdevice fmod
issues.body:
Fixes #11986.

`%` on floats lowers `arith.remf` to `llvm.frem`, and NVPTX has no frem instruction, so LLVM expands it inline as `a - trunc(a/b) * b` (verified on Triton's pinned LLVM build: `div.rn` / `cvt.rzi` / `fma.rn`). The expansion is sign-lossy at the exact-zero remainder (`-0.0 % 3.0` computes `-0.0 + 0.0 = +0.0` through the fused multiply-add, where fmod semantics and the Triton interpreter both require `-0.0`), and as peterbell10 pointed out it does not handle any edge cases or cover the full input range, since NVPTX lacks the libcall path LLVM normally uses for `frem` and falls back to this ad-hoc sequence.

This PR now follows that advice: on the NVIDIA backend `arith.remf` lowers to `__nv_fmodf` (f32) / `__nv_fmod` (f64) from libdevice, via the same `appendOrGetExternFuncOp` mechanism the extern elementwise math calls use, and libdevice is already linked into every NV compilation. libdevice fmod puts the dividend's sign on the result and handles NaN/inf/denormal inputs. An earlier revision of this PR fixed only the zero-sign case by following `llvm.frem` with `llvm.copysign`; that is dropped in favor of the full-domain fix.

On precision gating: triton has no fast-math attribute on `arith.remf` (unlike div, which has dedicated `tt.precise_divf`/`tt.approx_divf` ops), so there is no opt-out fast path to preserve. The perf delta should be small either way: `fmodf` is the same divide / truncate / multiply-and-subtract sequence as the expansion it replaces, just written in libdevice bitcode, and frem is a rare op in hot paths.

On NVIDIA, f16/bf16 are promoted to f32 by `semantic.py` and therefore take the same libdevice `__nv_fmodf` path; other backends keep the generic `llvm.frem` lowering.

Testing on current head `733ec2e7f41c`: the new lit case `remf_lowers_to_libdevice_fmod` in `test/Conversion/divide-by-0.mlir` asserts `arith.remf` becomes `llvm.call @__nv_fmodf`. The full `test/Conversion` suite is 85/85, plus `test/TritonGPU/fpsan.mlir` and `test/TritonNVIDIAGPU` (24/24). `clang-format --dry-run --Werror` and `git diff --check` pass. A separate October 10 registration merge had replaced rather than retained `SIToFPOpConversion` next to `RemFOpConversion`; the current head restores both registrations. Rebuilding the unmodified head first made `divide-by-0.mlir` pass while the existing `sitofp` coverage in `tritongpu_to_llvm.mlir` failed, then the two-line registration restoration made both targets pass. This avoided treating a stale local binary as evidence.

External GPU evidence is explicitly separated by head: on the earlier `dcf47079b`, a T4 matrix reported 144 mismatches on main versus 0 with the fmod change across the float special-value grid, and exposed the independent integer-cast registration failure. The registration fix is now included in `733ec2e7f41c`, but no new GPU run has been claimed for that later head; a T4 integer-conversion matrix re-run has been requested. No on-GPU execution was run locally.

issues.title: [NVIDIA] Lower more operations through LLVM and NVVM
issues.body:
Replace inline PTX with LLVM/NVVM operations and intrinsics where they preserve semantics and generate equivalent or better SASS:

- **Square roots:** `math.sqrt` → `llvm.sqrt` with `afn`; `math.rsqrt` → NVVM `rsqrt`.
- **Packed arithmetic:** FP16/BF16/FP32 add, subtract, and multiply, plus FP16/BF16 FMA → LLVM vector operations; FP16/BF16 min/max → `llvm.minimumnum` / `llvm.maximumnum`. Keep packed FP32 FMA in PTX to avoid register spills from instruction sinking.
- **FP8 conversions** use NVVM conversion ops and LLVM arithmetic, shuffles, and `copysign`. On SM89 and newer, the FP8-to-BF16 fallback uses `llvm.fptrunc.round` from #12237.
- **Integer and BF16 casts:** selected `i1` → FP16/BF16, signed `i8` → BF16, and BF16 → FP32 paths → LLVM selects, casts, and bit operations.
- **Global memory:** unpredicated default-cache tensor loads/stores → LLVM `load` / `store`. Keep scalar loads in PTX to avoid a ptxas FP8-reduction miscompile.
- **Atomics:** unpredicated scalar add, floating-point add, bitwise operations, signed/unsigned min/max, and exchange → LLVM `atomicrmw`; shared wrapping increments → `atomicrmw uinc_wrap`.
- **Compare-and-swap:** unpredicated 32-/64-bit CAS and instrumentation lock acquisition → LLVM `cmpxchg`.
- **Async memory:** eligible global-to-shared copies → NVVM `cp.async`; unpredicated scalar async shared stores → `llvm.nvvm.st.async`.

Preserve predication, rounding, memory ordering, and synchronization scopes. Retain PTX fallbacks for unsupported or regressing forms.

Remove the legacy SM75 MMA lowering in a separate preceding commit. Triton [documents NVIDIA support starting at compute capability 8.0](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/blob/8627ec5be64b6d5767edf313668de2e145a2718b/README.md#compatibility), and [Gluon’s `mma_v2` requires the Ampere `[2, 0]` layout](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/blob/8627ec5be64b6d5767edf313668de2e145a2718b/python/triton/experimental/gluon/language/nvidia/ampere/__init__.py#L117). The old SM75 `[2, 1]` path was still reachable when explicitly targeted; this removes that unsupported functionality.

issues.title: [LLVM] Update LLVM to 18f9e623
issues.body:
Update the consumed LLVM SDK to [`18f9e623e4c8`](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/commit/18f9e623e4c891ba31ff817c07197707ac9bc593), build 2, which includes the NVPTX `llvm.fptrunc.round` implementation. All eight checksums come from the successful [post-merge SDK build](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/actions/runs/38491954898) triggered by #12262; all eight published archives are available. Build 2 disables the optional LibLZMA dependency so Linux consumers configure without liblzma development files.

The LLVM/MLIR update requires these compatibility changes:

- Select NVPTX's `shortptr` ABI and preserve `enable_fp_fusion` through contraction flags.
- Pass the new `pzo` operand as `false` to NVVM FP32-to-FP16/BF16 and packed FP4 conversion intrinsics, preserving signed zero.
- Use the typed `LLVM::UMulHOp`, the updated pass APIs, and the new inline-assembly convergence argument.
- Place AMD named barriers in their dedicated address space, 15, and update their compile-only tests.
- Parse and restore LLVM TableGen library options alongside `cl::opt`, so MIR dump/reload honors codegen start/stop points and scheduler settings.
- Serialize alias-scope domains in the format supported by the independently pinned AMD code generator, preserving explicit alias/noalias relationships. Drop only the newer implicit disjoint-scope guarantee at that handoff.
- Preserve Triton's existing assembly syntax through MLIR's legacy-properties setting and keep supported attribute-dictionary builder deprecations as warnings.
- Refresh affected lit expectations for LLVM/MLIR assembly and PTX printing.

Rebased onto `2122e24efc`. Preserve upstream's `disable_lsr` option alongside the new LLVM ABI handling. Update the rebased barrier-printing expectations and remove the obsolete `llc -fp-contract=off` argument.

Validation on Brix GB300 at `f8ee3411f9`, with the published Ubuntu ARM64 build-2 SDK and `CMAKE_DISABLE_FIND_PACKAGE_LibLZMA=TRUE`:

- Native rebuild after the full build including Proton; verified the SDK archive checksum, configured SDK path, changed source hashes, Python package path, and AMD code-generator revision (`6bc4aaf6641c-3`).
- AMD code-generation and scheduler pytest suites: 25 passed, 2 GPU-only tests skipped. Reproduced the alias-domain failure before the fix; added coverage for named/anonymous domains, optional descriptions, and both disjoint flag values.
- `make test-lit`: 305 passed, 2 unsupported. The FP4 regression now translates through LLVM IR to PTX on SM100a.
- `make test-cpp`: 312 passed.
- Compiler-only, LLVM-option/ABI, LSR, BF16 rounding, and multiply-high pytest coverage: 89 passed.
- FP32-to-FP16/BF16 downcast tests: 4 passed.
- Direct FP4 packing test: 1 passed, covering ties, saturation, nibble order, and signed zero.
- Full `triton_kernels/tests/test_mxfp.py`: 172 passed.
- Pre-commit checks passed.

Follow-up validation on Brix GB300 at `df95c2e67c`:

- 313 native tests and 305 lit tests passed (2 unsupported).
- 33 AMD code-generation/scheduler tests passed (2 GPU-only tests skipped), including eight MIR round trips across gfx90a, gfx942, gfx950, and gfx1250 with machine scheduling both enabled and disabled.
- 74 compiler-option and compile-only tests passed.
- The CDNA5 compile-only suite passed at `8b935844c4`: 994 passed, 113 skipped.

[Full CI](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/actions/runs/38986951213) passed all 11 jobs at `df95c2e67c`: AMD gfx90a, gfx942, gfx950 (both ROCm configurations), gfx1250 emulation, NVIDIA A100/H100/GB200, macOS, formatting, and runner preparation. The NVIDIA conversion pattern is stacked on this pin update in #12237.

issues.title: [NVIDIA] Account for BF16 mixed-precision adds in the vectorizer
issues.body:
BF16-to-FP32 accumulation chains are currently costed as ordinary FP32 additions because `isFusedHalfAddition` only recognizes FP16 extensions. On SM100, this can select packed FP32 additions that retain separate BF16 conversions instead of folding them into mixed-precision adds.

Recognize BF16 extensions when computing the scalar addition-chain cost. The predicate remains restricted to FP32 `FAdd`; FMA operand-type matching is unchanged.

Add regression coverage for BF16 accumulation, both FP16/BF16 FMA factor orders, and same-type FMA controls. The mixed-factor cases retain their conversions and use ordinary FP32 FMA.

Validation:
- Full compiler lit suite: 305 passed, 2 unsupported plugin tests.
- 48 GB200 numerical/codegen cases passed, covering both factor orders, contraction enabled/disabled, scalar and packed layouts, and FMA followed by BF16 accumulation. None of the 24 mixed-factor cases emitted `FHFMA`.
- Pre-commit checks passed.

issues.title: [BACKEND] Compute bf16x3/bf16x6 dots with K < 16 exactly in fp32
issues.body:
Fixes #12252.

`tl.dot` with `input_precision="bf16x3"` or `"bf16x6"` on fp32 operands and K=8 returned exactly twice the product. The frontend admits fp32 dots with K as small as 8, and F32DotTC splits them into bf16 dots that keep the same K. Those splits sit below the 16-bit minimum the MMA path assumes (`K >= 256 / 16 = 16`): `supportMMA` guards K for MMAv3 and MMAv5 but never for MMAv2, so on Ampere-class targets the undersized dots convert to mma anyway. The MMAv2 operand layout then repeats the K elements across the instruction's K lanes and every result comes out doubled.

When the fp32 dot has K < 16, the pass now skips the split and marks the dot IEEE instead. The FMA path computes it exactly in fp32, which is strictly more accurate than the requested approximation, and the 16-bit K invariant that the AccelerateMatmul `minBitwidth` comment relies on holds again.

Both backends run `add_f32_dot_tc`; on AMD the same undersized splits would previously be emitted for K = 8, and exact fp32 is correct there too.

Tests: added a K=8 case to `test/TritonGPU/bf16x3-matmul.mlir` pinning that no splits are emitted and the dot keeps default (IEEE) precision. Ran the lit sweep locally: `test/TritonGPU` (139), `test/Triton` (14), `test/Analysis` (10), `test/Conversion` (85), all pass. No GPU on this machine, so the end-to-end numeric check from the issue was not rerun on hardware; the lit test pins the IR-level contract that no undersized bf16 dot reaches the MMA lowering.

issues.title: [AMD][gfx1250] Lower math.fma to packed FMA
issues.body: Generalize PackedArithOpConversion to pack an arbitrary number of operands and register it for math::FmaOp on gfx1250, so gl.fma / tl.fma on f32 and bf16 lower to <2 x T> llvm.fma and select v_pk_fma_f32 / v_pk_fma_bf16 instead of scalar (dual-issue) FMAs.

issues.title: [BC-breaking][Frontend] Fix FP8 ops by casting to FP16
issues.body:
We fixes a couple things:
- cast `float8e4b15` to fp64 now cast to `fp64` (it wasn't doing so earlier lol)
- abs(NaN) == NaN for NUZ types (before it was 0)
- Fix LLVM lowering of `reduce/assotive_scan` when `fp8` types are present
- Order-independent casting rules for ternary operators like `fma` or `clamp`

The new casting rules are as follows (see they mostly affect `fp8`).
They are BC-breaking in the sense that some `fp8` expressions were magically working when one of the inputs was a constexpr. Now the inference rules are uniform for constexpr and runtime values.

### Binary arithmetic

Apply these rules from top to bottom. Division and modulo are handled separately below.

| Operand types | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Either is FP64 | FP64 | FP64 |
| Either is FP32 | FP32 | FP32 |
| Either is FP16 | FP16 | FP16 |
| Both are BF16 | BF16 | BF16 |
| One is BF16 and the other reaches this row | FP32 | FP32 |
| Both are the same FP8 format | FP8† | **FP16** |
| Two different FP8 formats | FP16 | FP16 |
| FP8 + integer ≤8 bits, including bool | Error | **FP16** |
| FP8 + integer >8 bits | Error | **FP32** |
| Both are integers | Wider type; unsigned wins equal-width ties | Same |

†The frontend selected FP8. General runtime arithmetic then failed lowering by selecting `fp_op(i8, i8)`, but constant-folded expressions could compile and return FP8-rounded results.

### Operation-specific rules

| Operation | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Matching-FP8 comparison | Compare using FP8 operands†; return bool | **Compare using FP16 operands; return bool** |
| `where`, matching FP8 alternatives | Preserve FP8 | Preserve FP8 |
| `where`, FP8/integer alternatives | Error | **FP16 for ≤8-bit integers; otherwise FP32** |
| Floating `/`, `%`, `fdiv` | FP32; preserve FP64 | Same |
| Integer `/` | FP32; reject mixed signedness | Same |
| Integer `//`, `%` | Integer computation; reject mixed signedness | Same |
| FP8 unary negation | FP8† | **FP16** |
| FP8 `abs` | FP8 | FP8 |

The `where` condition does not participate in the alternatives' dtype promotion. FNUZ `abs` also preserves NaN instead of converting it to zero.

### Weak scalars

Python literals and `constexpr` values follow the kind hierarchy `bool < integer < floating point`. A loaded scalar tensor participates fully despite having shape `()`.

| Rule | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Scalar kind is lower than or equal to tensor kind | Scalar dtype does not influence promotion | Same |
| Scalar kind is higher than tensor kind | Scalar participates using its inferred dtype | Same |
| Materialize scalar operands | Use the final computation dtype | Same |
| Arithmetic other than division/modulo, with an FP8 tensor and a lower/equal-kind scalar | FP8 computation† | **FP16 computation** |

### Ternary `fma` and `clamp`

| Step | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Combine tensor dtypes | Fold left to right | **Consider every original tensor pair, then combine their results** |
| Handle weak scalars | Combine separately, then apply weak-scalar precedence | Same |
| Final FP8 dtype | Preserve FP8† | **Widen to FP16** |
| Cast operands | Cast directly to final dtype | Same |

The all-pairs change affects three tensor operands, including scalar-shaped tensors. It can change previously successful FP16 computations to FP32 when another original operand pair requires FP32. Previously, operand order could change the dtype or whether promotion succeeded.

### `sum`, `cumsum`, and `cumprod`

| Input or explicit request | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Explicit non-FP8 dtype | Requested dtype | Same |
| Explicit FP8 dtype | Select FP8† | **Error** |
| FP8 input, no explicit dtype | Select FP8† | **FP16** |
| Signed integer narrower than 32 bits | int32 | Same |
| Unsigned integer narrower than 32 bits | uint32 | Same |
| Other inputs | Input dtype | Same |

issues.title: [triton_kernels] Support tiled storage for persistent ragged-K matmul
issues.body:
Allow matrix producers to write tiled values and pass them to the ordinary `matmul` API without repacking or a separate launcher. `TiledLayout` describes the storage encoding, the existing TMA builder creates its five-dimensional descriptor, and the persistent kernel loads its tiles directly.

The initial matmul support is limited to aligned, persistent ragged-K TMA operations with one tile along the contiguous dimension. Unsupported descriptor shapes and noncontiguous encoded storage are rejected.

Validation on Blackwell: 28 tests passed, covering exact layout round trips, retained output buffers, either or both tiled operands, BF16/FP32 outputs, accumulation, and an empty slice. The same 28 tests pass with the upstream explicit bias-FMA fix (`0d45e109ad9e7d3dd5bf11b961fd590a2368a160`) included in this branch.

```
pytest -s --tb=short \
  python/triton_kernels/tests/test_tensor.py::test_tiled_layout_roundtrip \
  python/triton_kernels/tests/test_matmul.py::test_k_ragged_tiled_values
```
